gaps.sentence: Our guide was highly ___ and had climbed the mountain five times.
gaps.explanation: highly experienced is the standard collocation; 'highly' combines with participial adjectives.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: They ___ a lot of business with companies in Asia.
gaps.explanation: do business with somebody is the fixed expression for commercial activity.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ your seats; the performance is about to begin.
gaps.explanation: take your seats is the formal way of asking people to sit down.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: The boy knew it was wrong to ___ lies.
gaps.explanation: tell a lie / tell lies is the fixed collocation; a base verb is needed after 'to'.

gaps.sentence: Let me ___ a look at that cut on your arm.
gaps.explanation: take a look (at something) is the fixed collocation for examining something briefly.

gaps.sentence: Why don't we ___ lunch together on Friday?
gaps.explanation: have lunch is the standard collocation for eating lunch.
